RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the August 11, 2006/Sravana 20, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;
Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Small Scale Industries; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Survival of khadi products
*261. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of AGRO AND RURAL
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) the major threats for khadi products
and the measures undertaken to protect
those products from such threats;
(b) whether khadi industry would
survive and succeed in the absence of
concessions and assistance under rebate and
subsidy schemes; and
(c)  what are the measures and means to
prevent spurious products being produced
and sold in the name of khadi?
Medicine prices in tax holiday States
*262. SHRI PRASANTA
CHATTERJEE: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred
Question 3682 given in the Rajya Sabha on
the 19th May, 2006 and state:
(a) whether it is a fact that
manufacturing companies are free to fix the
MRP of drugs manufactured in tax-exempt
States;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
companies are supplying drugs
manufactured in tax-exempt States to gain
higher margins of profit; and
(c) whether Government would ensure
that drugs produced in both tax-exempt
States and non-exempt States are sold to
consumers on the same MRP?
Production and distribution of
genetically modified potato
†*263. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Committee of Ministry
of Environment and Forests have cleared
the new variety of  G.M. (Genetically
Modified) potato; and
(b) if so, the scheme of Government for
production and distribution of this seed?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

82
Beautification of Bhubaneswar
railway station
*264. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to beautify
the Bhubaneswar railway station, develop
more railway stations and improve
passenger amenities on ECoR;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the action plan of Government to
augment the line capacity works of  ECoR
to handle increased freight traffic in the
coming years?
Maintenance of public amenities on
railway stations
*265. SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the steps being taken to ensure the
cleanliness and maintenance of public
amenities on railway stations;
(b) whether any system has been
created to rate the stations on the basis
of cleanliness and upkeep of public
amenities;
(c) whether any system has been created
to fix the responsibility on concerned
officers for non-compliance of quality
amenities on stations; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Medical colleges in Nagaland
*266. SHRI T.R. ZELIANG: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have proposed
to set up medical colleges in Nagaland;
and
(b) if so, the steps taken in this regard?
AIDS cases in Uttar Pradesh
*267. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the largest number of AIDS patients are
there in our country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise,
particularly in Uttar Pradesh, gender-
wise;
(c) the main reasons for spread of such
fatal disease in the country and delay in
taking appropriate action for the protection
of the public; and
(d) the steps now proposed to be taken
for eradication of this disease?
Target for coverage under micro
irrigation
*268. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Task Force on Micro
Irrigation had recommended the coverage
of three million hectares under micro
irrigation in the country during the Tenth
Five Year Plan;

83
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the extent to which the said
target has been achieved, so far;
(c) whether Government have made
adequate allocation for that purpose; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Vaccine for bird flu
*269. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Indian Council of
Agricultural Research has developed an
indigenous vaccine against the deadly disease
'bird flu'; and
(b) if so, by when the vaccine is likely
to be available on commercial scale and how
its market price would compare to the price
of imported vaccine for the disease?
Exclusion of poor from PDS
*270. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Planning Commission
during the year 2005, after an evaluation of
Public Distribution System, found that 57
per cent of the poor had been actually
excluded from PDS;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken to rectify the above;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
return to the universal PDS; and
(d) the number of people covered under
targeted PDS for the last five years, State-
wise, year-wise and category-wise?
Decline in the number of wild
animals
†*271. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that population
of wild animals is continuously declining
since last few years;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have initiated
any concrete step in this regard; and
(d) whether Government are also
proposing to amend the Wild Life
(Protection) Act, 1972, with a view to take
stern steps?
Increase in the prices of medicines
†*272. SHRI DILIP SINGH JUDEV:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) the increase in percentage, witnessed
in the prices of medicines during the last
three financial years;
(b) whether permission has been sought
from Government for increasing the price
of any of the medicines;
(c) if so, the names of such medicines
alongwith the details of the permission
granted for the price rise; and
(d) the details of medicines whose prices
have either come down or have been reduced
during the last three years?

84
Hoarding of foodgrains by traders to
create artificial scarcity
*273. SHRI AMAR SINGH:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
huge quantity of foodgrains including pulses
and sugar have been purchased by traders
during the last three months and kept in
their stores so as to create its artificial
scarcity which has resulted in the abnormal
rise in its prices;
(b) if so, the approximate quantity of
foodgrains which has been purchased by
them; and
(c) whether Government had conducted
any raid in this connection and if so, the
details thereof and if not, the reasons
therefor?
Making HIV test mandatory before
marriage
*274. SHRI SHANTARAM
LAXMAN NAIK: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
make HIV test mandatory before marriage;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the names of States, if any, which
have made such a test mandatory?
Curbing the menace of counterfeit,
fake, spurious and contraband
products
*275. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the
Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the details and market share of
counterfeit, fake, spurious and contraband
products of various branded items;
(b) the loss that occurs to Government
and the industry due to such spurious
items; and
(c) the action taken to curb the menace?
Surprise inspections by MCI
*276. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Medical Council of
India (MCI) has inspected a number of
medical colleges to judge their suitability
for medical education;
(b)  whether it is a fact that MCI
conducts such inspections with surprise
and suddenness;
(c) if so, whether this policy of surprise
and suddenness is un-productive;
(d) whether it is also a fact that MCI is
selective about the secrecy and suddenness
of such visits; and
(e) the steps proposed to scrap this
archaic and highly un-professional style of
conducting inspections by MCI?

85
Lack of rainfall
*277. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that lack of rainfall
in the Northern States has become a concern
as rice and other crops are likely to be
affected; and
(b)  if so, the action Government
propose to take to tackle the situation?
Joint venture projects of Railways
*278. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Railways propose to enter
into joint ventures with various States for
different rail projects;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of such projects which
are located in Orissa?
Promotion of animal husbandry in
Rajasthan
*279. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the total cattle, category-wise, in
Rajasthan and plan of Government for
promotion of animal husbandry in
Rajasthan;
(b) the extent of success achieved in
this regard;
(c) whether Government are aware that
Rajasthan is a State where animal
husbandry is primarily adopted as an
occupation and hence special schemes
should be run;
(d) if so, the details of the schemes and
the funds allocated, so far, scheme-wise;
(e) the achievement and the percentage
of success of these schemes;
(f) whether any new special project has
been formulated or proposed to be
formulated in view of the geographical and
environmental situation of the State; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Development of western corridor from
JNPT to Delhi
*280. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government plan to
develop western corridor from JNPT to
Delhi via Vadodara-Ahmedabad-Palampur-
Jaipur;
(b)  if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
